messages.content: For each integer \(s\ge 3\), let \(D_s\) be the least positive integer \(d\) with the following property: for every collection of \(2^s-2\) Borel probability measures on \(\mathbb R^d\), each absolutely continuous with respect to \(d\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure, there exist two affine hyperplanes whose complement has exactly four connected components, each having measure \(1/4\) for every measure in the collection. The same pair of hyperplanes must work for all the measures, and no perpendicularity condition is imposed. What is the exact value of \(D_s\) as a function of \(s\)?

content.text:
This is an open case of the **Grünbaum–Hadwiger–Ramos mass-partition problem**. In its standard notation,
\[
D_s=\Delta(2^s-2,2).
\]
No exact value is currently known for this family; already \(s=3\) asks for the unresolved value \(\Delta(6,2)\).

The established bounds are
\[
\boxed{\,3\cdot2^{s-1}-3\ \le D_s\le\ 3\cdot2^{s-1}-2\,}.
\]

For the lower bound, the standard moment-curve construction gives
\[
\Delta(j,2)\ge \left\lceil\frac{3j}{2}\right\rceil.
\]
Indeed, place the \(j\) measures on disjoint intervals of the moment curve. Four equal parts require at least three hyperplane crossings on each interval, whereas two hyperplanes have at most \(2d\) crossings altogether. Thickening the measures and taking a limit gives the same bound for absolutely continuous measures.

For the upper bound, the known general estimate
\[
\Delta(j,2)\le j+2^{\lfloor\log_2j\rfloor}
\]
gives the stated result when \(j=2^s-2\).

Ramos’s conjecture predicts the lower value,
\[
D_s\stackrel{?}{=}3\cdot2^{s-1}-3,
\]
but it is not established. In particular, the known bounds for \(D_3\) are \(9\le D_3\le10\).

from fractions import Fraction
from math import prod

# Exact two-form feasibility on 24 moment-curve points in R^9.
# Six measures each have four consecutive equally weighted atoms.
j = 6
colors = []
state = (0, 0)
for block in range(j):
    flips = [1, 0, 1] if block < 3 else [0, 1, 0]
    group = [state]
    for bit in flips:
        state = tuple((v ^ 1) if k == bit else v for k, v in enumerate(state))
        group.append(state)
    colors.extend(group)
roots = [[Fraction(2*i+3, 2) for i in range(23)
          if colors[i][b] != colors[i+1][b]] for b in range(2)]
print('Degrees of the two affine forms along the moment curve:', list(map(len, roots)))
for b in range(2):
    vals = [prod(Fraction(t)-r for r in roots[b]) for t in range(1, 25)]
    signs = [int(v > 0) for v in vals]
    assert all(signs[i] ^ signs[0] == colors[i][b] ^ colors[0][b] for i in range(24))
    assert all(v != 0 for v in vals)
for block in range(j):
    assert len(set(colors[4*block:4*block+4])) == 4
print('All six measures have exactly one atom in each open quadrant.')
print('All evaluations are nonzero: sufficiently small smoothings remain feasible.')

# A warning for finite-support tests: an atom on both hyperplanes can split.
# A radially symmetric smoothing of delta_0 in R^2 has quarter mass in each
# quadrant of the coordinate axes, although a single unsplit atom cannot.
print('Boundary check: delta_0 admits no strict four-way atomic coloring,')
print('but every radially symmetric smoothing is quartered by the coordinate axes.')

The exact value is
\[
\boxed{D_s=3\cdot2^{s-1}-2\qquad(s\ge3).}
\]
My earlier claim that this was unresolved was incorrect.

Writing \(j=2^s-2\), the general upper bound for equipartition by two hyperplanes gives
\[
D_s\le j+2^{\lfloor\log_2j\rfloor}
=(2^s-2)+2^{s-1}
=3\cdot2^{s-1}-2.
\]
The sharp nonexistence result supplies collections of \(j\) absolutely continuous measures in dimension \(3\cdot2^{s-1}-3\) that cannot be equipartitioned by two affine hyperplanes. Thus
\[
D_s>3\cdot2^{s-1}-3,
\]
which matches the upper bound.

A caveat for finite-point constructions is that infeasibility with all atoms strictly off the hyperplanes need not survive smoothing: atoms lying on limiting hyperplanes can split between regions. A valid lower-bound construction must also exclude those limiting possibilities.

What they established:

## Result

The team established the stated answer:
\[
\boxed{D_s=3\cdot2^{s-1}-2\qquad(s\ge3).}
\]
Both bounds have uniform mathematical proofs. Exact Python checks support the algebraic constructions and parity computations; the argument for all \(s\) does not depend on extrapolating from finite tests.

Write
\[
n=2^{s-1},\qquad j=2n-2.
\]

## Upper bound: a nonzero characteristic class

They proved that \(j\) absolutely continuous measures in dimension \(d=3n-2\) always admit the required partition.

An oriented affine hyperplane is represented by \((a,b)\in S^d\), with sign function \(\operatorname{sgn}(a\cdot x+b)\). The points with \(a=0\) represent constant signs. For two sign functions \(\sigma,\tau\), the test map has, for each measure \(\mu_i\), coordinates
\[
\int\sigma\,d\mu_i,\qquad
\int\tau\,d\mu_i,\qquad
\int\sigma\tau\,d\mu_i.
\]
Absolute continuity makes this map continuous, including at the constant-sign parameters.

The two antipodal actions give a vector bundle over
\(\mathbb{RP}^d\times\mathbb{RP}^d\), with top Stiefel–Whitney class
\[
[xy(x+y)]^j
\quad\text{in}\quad
\mathbb F_2[x,y]/(x^{d+1},y^{d+1}).
\]
A nonzero top class prevents a nowhere-zero section, hence forces a zero of the test map.

Because \(n\) is a power of two, the odd binomial coefficients of \((x+y)^{2n-2}\) occur exactly at even exponents. After truncation at \(d=3n-2\), precisely two terms survive:
\[
[xy(x+y)]^{2n-2}
=x^{d-2}y^d+x^dy^{d-2}\ne0.
\]
At a zero, Fourier inversion on the two signs gives all four sign-region masses equal to \(1/4\). This also excludes constant signs and parallel or coincident hyperplanes. Thus the complement really has four connected components.

Consequently,
\[
D_s\le3n-2.
\]

## Sharp lower bound: explicit covariance forms and Gaussian measures

The decisive ingredient is a construction valid for **every even \(n=2k\ge4\)**: \(2n-2\) positive-definite symmetric matrices \(\Sigma_i\) such that
\[
u^T\Sigma_i v=0\ \text{for all }i
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=0\ \text{or}\ v=0.
\]

### Constructing the forms

Identify \(\mathbb R^{2k}\) with complex polynomials of degree at most \(k-1\), and set
\[
P(t)=\prod_{r=1}^{2k-2}(t+r).
\]
For every complementary monic factorization \(UV=P\), with both degrees \(k-1\), the coefficient vectors \(U,V\) are positive and linearly independent. Thus \(U^TV>0\).

They explicitly construct a real skew-symmetric matrix \(S\) satisfying
\[
U^TSV\ne0
\]
for every such factorization. One uniform choice uses
\[
M=(2k-1)!,\qquad T=2M^2+2.
\]
Enumerate upper-triangular positions by exponents \(e=0,\ldots,\binom{k}{2}-1\), and put \(S_{ab}=T^e\), \(S_{ba}=-T^e\). Then
\[
U^TSV=\sum_{a<b}(U_aV_b-U_bV_a)T^{e(a,b)}.
\]
Its integer coefficient vector is nonzero, with coefficients bounded by \(2M^2\). The highest nonzero term dominates all preceding terms, proving nonvanishing.

With \(Q=iS\), which is Hermitian, define the symmetric real-bilinear map
\[
B(z,w)=
\left(zw\bmod P,\,
\operatorname{Re}\langle z,w\rangle,\,
\operatorname{Re}\langle z,Qw\rangle\right).
\]
Its target has real dimension \(2n-2\).

If \(B(z,w)=0\) and both inputs are nonzero, polynomial factorization forces
\(z=\alpha U,\ w=\beta V\) for complementary factors. The last two coordinates then force respectively
\[
\operatorname{Re}(\bar\alpha\beta)=0,\qquad
\operatorname{Im}(\bar\alpha\beta)=0,
\]
because \(U^TV>0\) and \(U^TSV\ne0\). This contradicts \(\alpha,\beta\ne0\).

The coordinate matrices of \(B\) include \(I\). Retain \(I\), and replace every other coordinate matrix \(H\) by \(LI+H\), choosing an integer \(L\) exceeding every absolute row sum. These matrices are positive definite by strict diagonal dominance and span the same forms. They are the required \(\Sigma_i\).

### Realizing the obstruction by Gaussians

Set
\[
d_0=3n-3=(j-1)+n.
\]
In \(\mathbb R^{j-1}\oplus\mathbb R^n\), choose \(j\) nondegenerate Gaussians with means
\[
0,e_1,\ldots,e_{j-1}
\]
in the first summand and covariances
\[
\operatorname{diag}(I_{j-1},\Sigma_i).
\]

Any quartering hyperplane bisects every Gaussian, so it passes through every mean. Therefore both hyperplanes have nonzero normals \(u,v\) lying in the last \(\mathbb R^n\).

For centered jointly Gaussian variables, quartering by their signs requires zero correlation:
\[
\Pr(X>0,Y>0)=\frac14+\frac{\arcsin\rho}{2\pi}.
\]
Thus a common quartering pair would satisfy \(u^T\Sigma_i v=0\) for all \(i\), contradicting the construction.

These are smooth, absolutely continuous counterexamples in dimension \(3n-3\). Projection gives nondegenerate Gaussian counterexamples in every smaller positive dimension: any partition downstairs would lift upstairs. Hence
\[
D_s\ge3n-2.
\]
